root_cause: The module-level tokenizer regex re_ansi in rich/ansi.py only matched OSC (ESC ] ... ESC \), a small set of single-char escapes ([(@-Z\-_]) and CSI sequences. Fp 'private' escapes ESC 0 .. ESC ? (0x30-0x3F, e.g. ESC 7 / ESC 8 save/restore cursor) matched nothing, so Text.from_ansi kept the raw ESC plus char in the plain text and Console re-emitted them, moving the cursor and garbling output.
best_solution: Add one new first alternative to re_ansi: `(?:\x1b[0-?])|` (non-capturing, so the osc/sgr capture groups and every downstream branch in _ansi_tokenize are untouched). When it matches, both groups are None, so the tokenizer yields an empty token and advances position past the 2-char escape, which strips it. Reasoning from the statement: it names the exact byte range \x1b0-\x1b? and says 'update the ANSI parser to ignore' them; the parser is the single regex feeding _ansi_tokenize, and the safest edit is an additive alternative rather than rewriting the existing character class (which carries the special-cased '(' used for charset designation ESC ( B).
acceptable_alternatives: Inserting 0-? into the existing single-char class while KEEPING '(' also works, e.g. `[(0-?@-Z\\-_]` (verified: ESC 7 is captured as sgr '7' and dropped; ESC ( still captured as '(' and the next char skipped). Any change must leave ESC ( B / ESC ( J stripping intact.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_ansi.py::test_strip_private_escape_sequences parametrized over each of '0123456789:;<=>?': Text.from_ansi(f'\x1b{code}x') printed via Console(force_terminal=True) inside capture() must produce exactly 'x\n'. Existing tests/test_ansi.py::test_decode_issue_2688 (ESC ( B / ESC ( J charset sequences stripped, e.g. '\x1b(BHallo' -> 'Hallo') must keep passing.
locating_signals: Title/body say 'ANSI parser', 'escape sequences', 'strip'; grep for 'ansi' leads to rich/ansi.py whose only parser is the re_ansi regex. Function/variable is not named in the statement, but the byte range (\x1b0-\x1b?) is given exactly and maps directly to a regex character range [0-?].
our_outcome_summary: All four configs failed (kaggle_env_pass v4/v6/v7/v8 = false; every run hit the 110-call cap at ~210-230 s). v4 and v7: empty patch, all 16 new parametrized tests fail with the ESC byte left in output. v6: only created tests/repro_issue.py (a repro test) and never edited rich/ansi.py, so the same 16 failures. v8: correct location and idea but rewrote the class `[(@-Z\\-_]` as `[0-?@-Z\\-_]`, i.e. REPLACED '(' with '0-?' instead of adding it; the 16 new tests pass but 4 pre-existing test_decode_issue_2688 cases now fail ('\x1b(BHallo' printed raw) because the charset-designation branch `if sgr == "("` can no longer fire. Running the existing tests/test_ansi.py once after the edit would have caught it.
generalizable_lesson: When editing a regex (especially a character class) make the change strictly additive: add a new alternative or append to the class, never retype or replace existing members, then diff old vs new pattern character by character; downstream code often special-cases individual captured characters (here '('). Always run the existing test file for the touched module before finishing, since a fix that passes the new behaviour but regresses old cases scores zero. Also, spend the call budget on the source edit first: a repro test file alone is not a fix.
